title: Bounded extremally disconnected cover of a profinite space
statement: Let $X$ be a profinite space, meaning a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space (an object of $\mathbf{Prof}$ as defined in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]) and $\lambda$ an infinite cardinal with $|X|\leq\lambda$. There exist a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space $T$ and a continuous surjection $u:T\to X$ such that $T$ is extremally disconnected (the closure of every open subset is open) and $|T|\leq 2^{2^\lambda}$.

source.place: Topology, Tag 090D, lemma-existence-projective-cover; Tag 090E, remark-size-projective-cover; quasi-compact Hausdorff extremally disconnected spaces are profinite

proof.text: Take $S$ to be the underlying set of $X$, and set $T=\mathcal U(S)$ with the topology of [lem-weil-pbc-ultrafilter-compact-hausdorff-basis]. This is a compact Hausdorff space, with clopen basic subsets $[A]$ for $A\subseteq S$. For $s\in S$, the family $p(s)=\{A\subseteq S:s\in A\}$ is a proper filter and is maximal: any strictly larger filter would contain a set omitting $s$, whose intersection with $\{s\}$ is empty. Thus $p(s)\in T$, and $p(s)\in[A]$ exactly when $s\in A$.

source.place: Tag 090D, lemma-existence-projective-cover, first proof paragraph: take the underlying discrete set and its Stone-Cech compactification. Tag 0908, section-stone-cech supplies the abstract compactification; the concrete ultrafilter realization used here is supplied by Mathlib/Topology/Compactification/StoneCech.lean, lines 54-99.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ultrafilter-continuous-extension] to the set map $f:S\to X$, $f(s)=s$. Its target $X$ is compact Hausdorff by hypothesis. We obtain a continuous $u:T\to X$ with $u(p(s))=s$ for every $s\in X$, which proves surjectivity (also when $X$ is empty).

source.place: Tag 090D, lemma-existence-projective-cover, first proof paragraph: factor the map from the underlying discrete set through its compactification

proof.text: We verify extremal disconnectedness directly from the basis of [lem-weil-pbc-ultrafilter-compact-hausdorff-basis]. For open $O\subseteq T$ put $A=\{s\in S:p(s)\in O\}$. If $F\in O$, choose $B\in F$ with $F\in[B]\subseteq O$. Then $B\subseteq A$ by the principal-ultrafilter membership formula, so $A\in F$. Hence $O\subseteq[A]$ and $\overline O\subseteq[A]$, since $[A]$ is closed. Conversely if $F\in[A]$, every basic neighbourhood $[B]$ of $F$ has $A\cap B\in F$ and therefore $A\cap B\ne\varnothing$. Choosing $s\in A\cap B$ gives $p(s)\in O\cap[B]$. Every neighbourhood of $F$ meets $O$, so $[A]\subseteq\overline O$. Thus $\overline O=[A]$ is open. This includes $O=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 090C, example-stone-Cech-discrete: extremal disconnectedness of the discrete Stone-Cech compactification; direct basis calculation in place of the projectivity argument

proof.text: The same clopen basis implies total disconnectedness: if distinct ultrafilters $F,G\in T$ lie in a subset $C$, some subset $A\subseteq S$ belongs to exactly one of the two families. Then $C\cap[A]$ and $C\setminus[A]$ are disjoint nonempty relatively open subsets with union $C$. Therefore $C$ is disconnected. Every connected subset of $T$ consequently has at most one point. Together with compactness and Hausdorffness from step 1 this makes $T$ profinite.

source.place: Tag 090C, example-stone-Cech-discrete, final sentence: discrete Stone-Cech compactification is profinite

proof.text: For the size estimate, each ultrafilter is literally a family of subsets of $S$, so $F\mapsto F$ injects $T$ into $\mathcal P(\mathcal P(S))$. Choose a set $L$ with $|L|=\lambda$ and an injection $j:S\hookrightarrow L$, using $|X|\leq\lambda$. Direct image $A\mapsto j(A)$ is injective on power sets, since $j^{-1}(j(A))=A$; taking direct images of families under this injection gives an injection $\mathcal P(\mathcal P(S))\hookrightarrow\mathcal P(\mathcal P(L))$. Thus $|T|\leq|\mathcal P(\mathcal P(L))|=2^{2^\lambda}$, where the equality identifies subsets with their characteristic functions twice. This uses only the definitions of cardinal inequality and exponentiation, and not an additional dense-subspace cardinal estimate. The empty set gives no ultrafilters and satisfies the same inequality.
